The air was thick with the scent of salt and diesel, a familiar perfume that clung to their clothes and hair. They had worked all day, hoisting containers onto the waiting trucks, their muscles aching from the repetitive motion of the levers. Now, the city lights began to flicker on, reflecting off the water like scattered diamonds. The old man paused, leaning against the railing, watching the last of the cargo ships disappear into the fog. He remembered when the harbour was a place of bustling activity, with sailors shouting orders and the air filled with the sound of hammers and laughter. Now, it was quieter, more somber. The silence was heavy, pressing against his ears. He wondered if the younger generation would ever understand the weight of the harbour's history, the stories etched into the rusted steel and the weathered wood.
